messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PDR-14358 fired for policy 'canary-oom-spike' — canary cluster model-serving-canary-7 experiencing pod OOMKills (>=12% error rate). See: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PDR-14358
liam: acked (on-call). I'm jumping in. Initial check: node pressure + frequent OOMKilled in canary pods.
sara: rel-2026-03-15-03 went to canaries at 02:14 UTC. It introduced a new quant kernel allocator — suspicious. Reproduced a single pod OOM locally with long sequences. Logs: ```Mar 15 02:17:03 model-serving-canary-7 kubelet[1234]: Container model-runtime OOMKilled
2026-03-15T02:17:02Z WARN runtime: allocation failed: requested 18446744073709551615 bytes
```
ops-bot: autoscaler triggered scale up x2 for canary-nodes but new pods scheduled show CrashLoopBackOff.
liam: running `kubectl describe pod model-runtime-abc123` shows eviction due to memory. Also seeing node fragmentation: pods can't place because large contiguous alloc needed.
sara: quick mitigation plan: (1) abort canary rollout via infra API to stop sending more traffic to canary, (2) scale stable to absorb load, (3) roll back canary to previous revision. I'll start rollback.
liam: aborting canary routing: `infractl traffic-set model-serving prod --selector=stable --percent=100 --reason="canary-ooms"` — executed. Traffic diverted.
cs_liaison: pinging support ops; preparing customer notification draft for affected sessions. Early estimate: ~4% of requests routed to canary window 02:14-02:20 UTC.
sara: initiating helm rollback: `helm rollback model-serving 42 --namespace prod` -> started. Also cordoning the canary nodes: `kubectl label node canary-7 cordon=temporary` to prevent rescheduling.
liam: metrics: p95 for chat-generation improved after diversion, error-rate for global dropped to <0.2%. Canary pods still OOMing on restart.
ops-bot: note: there were two distinct node types in canary pool, one with kernel-oz build that aligns with allocator change.
sara: looking at allocator code change: new contiguous buffer request for kv cache when sequences > 4096. That can blow memory on some instances. Opening PR to revert allocator path. Link: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8967 (revert quant-allocator).
liam: customer impact: flagged customers — starting outreach to top 10 accounts that hit generation timeouts. Nina from CS looped in.
cs_liaison: posted initial note to #support-escalations: "Small subset of requests to canary saw OOMs during rollout window; traffic diverted and rollback commenced. Will follow up with RCA and timeline."
sara: rollback succeeded at 02:23 UTC; replica sets stabilized. Watching memory graphs.
liam: verifying cluster health: all production stable replicas healthy at 02:26 UTC. Canary nodes isolated; no further OOMs observed on stable.
liam: creating short-lived mitigation: add automated canary abort: if canary OOM > 1% for 3m, abort and divert automatically. Filing infra GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/3122
ops-bot: reminder — rotation handoff scheduled at 03:00 UTC. liam will hand to sara if incident still open.
sara: quick debug note: the allocator uses a signed->unsigned cast leading to massive allocation on certain paths when neg lengths occur. Root cause appears to be edge-case in tokenizer output for some sequences. Adding guard.
liam: escalation decision: suppress PD escalation chain for now; we have traffic diverted and rollback. Reopen PD if errors persist above threshold.
sara: PR for revert merged at 02:47 UTC. CI green. Adding a unit test `test_allocator_negative_len_guard`.
liam: post-incident customer summary prepared and sent at 03:05 UTC. Offering SOC review for any customers that request more details.
nina: CS report: 6 inbound tickets from premium accounts, created SRs and applied temporary usage credits where SLA impacted.
sara: action items recorded: 1) hard revert merged, 2) add canary abort rule & test in infra (owner: liam), 3) add allocator guard + unit tests (owner: sara), 4) update release checklist for quant kernel changes (owner: eng-release).
liam: scheduling RCA meeting for 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC. Will draft timeline and collect logs.
incident-bot: Incident PDR-14358 marked mitigated -> closed at 03:20 UTC. Summary in PD: "canary rollout rel-2026-03-15-03 caused allocator behavior leading to OOMKills on canary pods; traffic diverted, rollback and revert applied; impacted small percentage of requests, customers notified."
cs_liaison: final: thanks team for fast triage. Posting postmortem link to #incidents when available. :thumbsup:
